text:
Predicates:
Winner(x, y) ::: x is the winner of y.
Participated(x, y) ::: x participated in y.
TieOnLeaderboard(y, z) ::: y is a tie on the leaderboard z.
FromBelgium(x) ::: x is from Belgium.
OnLeaderboard(x, y) ::: x is on the leaderboard y.
SixWayTie(y) ::: y is a six-way tie.
PeopleOnLeaderboard(y) ::: people are on the leaderboard y.
Premises:
Winner(Steinhauer, duMaurier1992) ::: Steinhauer was the winner of the 1992 du Maurier Classic.
Participated(Steinhauer, duMaurier1992) ::: Steinhauer participated in the 1992 du Maurier Classic.
∃x (TieOnLeaderboard(x, duMaurier1992) ∧ SixWayTie(x) ∧ ∃y (FromBelgium(y) ∧ OnLeaderboard(y, duMaurier1992) ∧ Participated(y, duMaurier1992))) ::: There was a six-way tie on the leaderboard, and one person in the tie was from Belgium.
Descampe is from Belgium and is on the leaderboard of the 1992 du Maurier Classic ::: FromBelgium(Descampe) ∧ OnLeaderboard(Descampe, duMaurier1992).
All people on the leaderboard of the 1992 du Maurier Classic participated in it ::: ∀x (OnLeaderboard(x, duMaurier1992) → Participated(x, duMaurier1992)).

Conclusion:
∃x (TieOnLeaderboard(x, duMaurier1992) ∧ FromBelgium(x) ∧ x = Descampe) ::: Descampe is in the six-way tie in the leaderboard of the 1992 du Maurier Classic.
